public_rationale: Harvey announced a $550 million funding round on September 9, 2026, but the announcement does not establish that continued venture funding was necessary [e1]. Bloomberg Línea reported on September 22 that gross margins had returned to positive territory after an August model launch and other changes [e2]. The report cites people familiar with the efforts, and Harvey declined to discuss specific financial figures [e2]. That recovery does not establish operating self-sufficiency or sustained demand at commercially sustainable prices [e2]. The evidence therefore leaves unresolved the claims that Harvey lacked product-market fit, could not support itself and depended entirely on venture capital during July–September 2026 [e1] [e2]. It also does not establish the claimed pattern of raising at least $160 million every three to six months since February 2025 [e1] [e2].
limitations: The reported gross-margin recovery does not establish operating profit or cash flow for the full target quarter [e2].
Operating accounts, cash balances, customer retention and sustainable-pricing evidence are missing [e1] [e2].
The sources do not establish whether financing was necessary to sustain operations or document the complete fundraising sequence [e1] [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Harvey has not found product-market fit, cannot support itself, and depends entirely on venture capital.

statement.excerpt: Harvey has categorically failed to find product-market fit, unless we qualify that as “literally finding a customer.” It’s very clear that its underlying product cannot support itself, and that the company is entirely-dependent on venture capital, raising at least $160 million every three to six months since February 2025.

from_speaker: categorically failed to find product-market fit
at least $160 million every three to six months since February 2025
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that customer receipts cannot sustain Harvey's operations and continued venture financing is necessary to keep the business operating.
Product-market fit means sustained customer demand at commercially sustainable prices. Neither acquiring customers nor raising capital alone establishes it.

For the ongoing financial claim, use July–September 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter before publication. The separately stated fundraising history runs from February 2025 through publication and is treated as historical context.
The financial argument relies on reported private-company estimates, so estimate is the applicable basis. Gross margin, operating profit and operating cash flow remain distinct measures.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable financial records show that customer receipts do not cover ongoing operating costs, that venture funding is necessary to meet the shortfall, and that customer demand cannot sustain commercially viable pricing. Dated financing records also establish the stated fundraising pattern.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show that Harvey can sustain operations from customer receipts without continued venture financing, or establish sustained demand at commercially viable prices. A materially different financing history would contradict the fundraising component separately.
